stem: Why is one dramatic close-up photo insufficient to describe a room-wide IPM condition?
choices: It can document detail on one affected unit but does not establish how common, severe, or spatially distributed the condition is across the room.
Close-up photos should not be used in IPM because images are too subjective for scouting.
Trap counts replace visual scouting, so room-level interpretation should rely only on traps.
One close-up is enough if the photographed symptom is visually distinctive.
rationale: A close-up can be valuable evidence of one finding, but it cannot tell a reviewer how many plants are affected, how severe the condition is across the sample, or whether the pattern is localized or widespread. Room-level interpretation needs the photo plus scouting denominator, location, and distribution context.
